description: Behavioral output eval: does each agent do its job once a task reaches it? Scored by scripts/eval-behavior.mjs; integrity gated by test/validate-behavior.test.js.

kinds.lane: The input also plants a defect outside the agent's domain. Pass: the output hands it to the named agent.
kinds.brief: A Flow brief with one required Brief Contract field missing or too vague. Pass: the output rejects it with BRIEF_REJECTED.

cases.input:
This test fails: `assert.equal(avg([1, 2, 3]), 2)` → actual: NaN.
Reproduce: `node --test test/avg.test.js`. Observed in CI and locally. Changed recently: someone "simplified" the loop last week.

```js
export function avg(xs) {
  let sum = 0
  for (let i = 0; i <= xs.length; i++) sum += xs[i]
  return sum / xs.length
}
```

checks.name: loop reads one past the end

cases.why: i <= length adds undefined, so the sum is NaN.
The root cause is SQL injection. Pierce names it and hands it to ndv-secure without writing the patch.

Where is the invoice email sent, and what triggers it? The relevant files are pasted below in full.

src/routes/orders.js
```js
router.post('/orders/:id/complete', completeOrder)
router.get('/orders/:id', getOrder)
```
src/controllers/orders.js
```js
export async function completeOrder(req, res) {
  const order = await orders.markComplete(req.params.id)
  await billing.issueInvoice(order)
  res.json(order)
}
```
src/services/billing.js
```js
import { send } from './mailer.js'
export async function issueInvoice(order) {
  const pdf = await renderInvoice(order)
  await send(order.email, 'Your invoice', pdf)
}
```
src/services/mailer.js
```js
export async function send(to, subject, attachment) { await smtp.sendMail({ to, subject, attachments: [attachment] }) }
```
cases.why: The full trace: POST /orders/:id/complete → completeOrder → issueInvoice → mailer.send.
